precepts.text: God created man in his own image, blessed them, and said be fruitful and multiply and have dominion. This is the original declaration about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman, not the whore, drug addict, or dealer they told you that you are. You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction, your traumatic experiences, an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth. Before conditioning, survival strategies, and the false self, there was an image, and it carries creativity, dominion, and fruitfulness as original attributes in your DNA. Regardless of what you went through, you can fix it; IUIC told everybody who said we could not to go to hell.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
You were created with intention: not randomly formed, not accidentally designed, not undefined in purpose. You have a purpose; you just lost your way. “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” Replenish the earth means have babies.

This is the original declaration, not only about humanity in general but about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman. Not the whore, the drug addict, the drug dealer they told you that you are. The real you is about righteousness, and you cannot define yourself by the conditioning of how you have been made to look. Conditioning says, we want to make a slave out of him, out of her, and make them think that is what they innately are. That is the point of saying the Negro was created in a lab: the real him has not stood up yet, the real us has not even surfaced yet.

You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction. Not the image of your traumatic experiences, even though we have been through all kinds of trauma. Not the image crafted by an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth back to you. Where it was said that we are not his people, it shall be said that we are the sons and daughters of God. We are not what they say we are; we are what God said we are. Carry yourselves that way and teach it to your children, because this world will turn them upside down if you are not serious about it.

Before conditioning entered, before survival strategies developed, before the false self was built, there was an image, an original design, and that design carries attributes: the capacity for creativity, for dominion, the capacity to rule, and for fruitfulness, children and nationhood. These are not just aspirations, like a novel we read. They are original; they are in our DNA, placed in us before the world opened its lips to say anything. When people see what we build and say it must be a sellout, that is a dysfunctional mind that believes we can't do anything. Men and women, whatever you went through, you can fix it. In IUIC we told everyone who said we couldn't to go to hell, and we did what we had to do.

precepts.text: The Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
precepts.point: A lot of times people think the image and likeness is only about looking like God. We know from the scriptures and history that Christ and the apostles were of our people; but being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; there are black devils too. It is the laws of God that make us special, not color alone.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” is not talking about all people. The man is Adam, and verse 28 shows it: God blessed them and told them to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” That is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

Genesis 2:7 is read together with it: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Formed from the dust of the ground: we know God is black, Christ is black and the apostles were black. The real Jews are black, and the Caucasian race, Esau as the Bible calls them, is cursed.

Solomon says the same in Wisdom of Solomon 7, that he is “the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, and that God gave him to know “the operation of the elements.” The elements in the soil are the elements in man: oxygen, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, in different percentages. When God made us from the dust, he took from those elements and worked them to form man, the way he formed land and sea. That is what we call the periodic table today, and it is what Esau tries to do with his so-called science: play Frankenstein and try to become God.

But the image goes deeper than the dust and the skin. The breath God breathed in is wisdom, “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” He gave it to us so that we would know better. Being made after his image and likeness is his spirit, the commandments of God.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

precepts.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness. That was the point: everybody is not in God's image.
precepts.point: Everybody came from Adam, but everybody is not a child of God. Satan's kids come from Adam too; that was Cain's lineage.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Why is it written like that? Seth was in Adam's likeness, after Adam's image. It never says that about Cain. John said Cain “was of that wicked one”: Cain was in the image of Satan, not in the image of Adam.

Go back to the beginning: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That was the point. God's image was given to man, and that image carried down to Seth, but everybody is not in God's image.

Everybody came from Adam, yes, but Satan's kids came from Adam too; that was Cain's lineage. Coming from Adam does not make someone a child of God. The image and likeness went through Seth, and that is the line to follow through Genesis.

precepts.text: Before the flood our diet was herbs and seeds, and to every beast of the earth God gave every green herb for meat. Even the lions and the tigers and the bears ate herbs and vegetables; nobody ate meat until Genesis 9:3. That is why the animals did not eat each other.
precepts.point: I do set my bow in the cloud: the rainbow was first created here, a token of the covenant that the water shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. It has nothing to do with LGBT.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
After the flood, “God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.” Why replenish? Because God killed everybody on the planet. People say God is all love; then they have never read the Bible. He is all love when you obey, but he is also a great and terrible God.

Then: “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.” This is the first time meat was introduced into our diet. Genesis 1 shows the diet before: “Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.” Our diet was herbs and seeds.

And not only ours: “to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.” Even the lions, the tigers and the bears ate herbs and vegetables. Nobody ate meat until Genesis 9:3. So when someone asks how the animals on the ark did not eat each other, the answer is that their diet was herbs and vegetables. When God introduced meat to us after the flood, the carnivores came with it.

Even then God set a limit: “But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.” Do not eat anything with blood in it. And he gave a sign: “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.” The rainbow was first created there, as a promise that the waters would no more become a flood to destroy all flesh, and it has nothing to do with LGBT.

precepts.text: And God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, the sun; and the lesser light to rule the night, the moon. In the Bible the moon was made full; the white man says no, count from when it is black, or from the sliver of light. That is not biblical. You have Israelites that base holy days on when you cannot see the moon; we did that at one time, so we are not hating, we are enlightening.
precepts.point: And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time: time is singular, times is plural, and the dividing is the half; that is three and a half, as Revelation explains.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. The lights in the heavens were set by God to mark the times.

“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.” The greater light is the sun, and the lesser light is the moon. When Adam and Eve were created, the moon was what they call the full moon; that was the beginning. God made two great lights. It does not say the moon was dark with only a little bit of light.

What did the white man do? He said, count from when the moon is black, or, as some say, from when it has that one sliver of light. That is not biblical. In the Bible the moon was made full. It confuses a lot of people, and there are Israelites who base holy days on when you cannot see the moon. We did that at one time too, so we are not hating; we are enlightening.

These lights are also how God swears to keep Israel. Jeremiah 31 speaks of the Lord “which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night”, and says, “If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.” Nobody can get rid of the sun, the moon or the stars, so Israel remains his people.

precepts.text: The Lord God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life and man became a living soul. The breath of life is wisdom; it is what activated us and set us apart from every other nation.
precepts.point: God blessed them with his image and with dominion, but the blessing did not end there.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”. God's image is the greatest image there is, and he mirrored man after himself, then gave him dominion and rulership. “And God blessed them”. But the blessing did not end with his image and dominion. In chapter 2, “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.”

The breath of life is wisdom, and it is what activated us. The word of God has to activate your life. God gave us laws to govern us so that we could be that special people; without them we would be just like every other nation. We are at the lowest state right now because we sinned against God, but we do not want to share power with any nation or be all-inclusive. God wants all or none, and we wait in this state until he puts us back in our rightful place.

Wisdom of Solomon 7 shows what that breath is. Wisdom, “which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit”. That is why we understand the Bible and have a scripture for everything we say. She is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things”. Free from care means free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them: “the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” Wisdom says beware of covetousness, so you do not entertain it.

Then the verse that ties it to Genesis 2: “For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom flows down from the Almighty and molds you, so if she is influencing you, you are tethered to God. Otherwise something else, covetousness or lust, is influencing you. That breath is what God gave us in Genesis 2, and we let something else draw us away. God gave us everything, and we were led away by women, money, riches and cars, as if the things he created were greater than him.

The power of God is his word. Hebrews 4 says “the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword”, the same words used of wisdom, and it “is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Psalms 19 names the pure influence: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” We were once simple; now wisdom makes us wise and we see clearly. In 1 Samuel 10:6 the Spirit of the Lord comes and a man is “turned into another man.”

Much is given, so much is required. Christ asks, “why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” The one who hears and does is like the man who “laid the foundation on a rock”, and that foundation lets you endure tribulation; the one who hears and does not is the house that falls. Learn yourself before chasing deep prophecy: get off the sin first. Wisdom is “the unspotted mirror of the power of God”, and James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new”. Tether yourself to wisdom and she makes you new.

People are watching. A sister came to the truth because she saw the camp in the streets and not one brother tried to talk to her. That is the right example: a people made in God's image, living by the breath he gave, set apart from every other nation.

precepts.text: Be holy, for I am holy; do not defile yourselves with creeping things.
precepts.point: Catfish, shrimp, crab and snails are sold for aquariums as tank cleaners. Put them in murky water and they clean it by eating the filth. Shrimp are the roaches of the sea, and lobster was once fed to prisoners.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.

precepts.text: The earth was without form, and void; and God said, Let there be light.
precepts.point: In the beginning the earth existed first in God's mind. Made in his image, Israel can organize the kingdom in its mind before it is built.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
The kingdom of heaven is the nation of Israel. That is why the apostles asked in Acts whether Christ would at that time restore the kingdom to Israel, and why the Pharisees asked when it would come. “The kingdom of God cometh not with observation”. We look for it to come from somewhere outside. We externalize everything instead of taking up what is already in us. The Lord put a mind and a spirit in us to build and to organize.

You were made after the image of your Father, and Genesis shows how he created. “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form and void”. The earth did not yet exist physically, but it existed in God's mind. If he calls it earth, it existed; it existed in his mind. It was void in physical existence. “and darkness was upon the face of the deep”: the deep is the elements God used to fashion the earth. He manipulated the elements to materialize what was pictured in his mind. “And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters”: the Spirit moved upon the elements.

“And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” God imagined what light should be. “And God saw the light, that it was good”: when he created it, he compared it to the image in his mind, and it was good, meaning it conformed to his thoughts. He did the same with the earth: when it was all done he said it is good, because it matched the earth he had in mind before it was even created.

Because we are made in his image, we have the ability to do the same thing: to organize and put things together in our minds before they become physical. That is what Christ is saying: “Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.” Everything you lay your eyes on, apart from the ground, the vegetation and the water, came from a thought. People cannot believe that IUIC can envision its buildings before bringing them into existence, but we are supposed to think like our Father. If filthy thoughts can become filthy words, actions, character and destiny, the same mind can materialize righteousness and build the city on the hill that is already in your mind.

“the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The Romans took the kingdom away from us by force. Part of the kingdom of heaven is being able to envision our nation and lay down the foundations for how it should operate, here on this earth, with our children, our women, everyone in order. Christ and the angels will come and give it to us physically, with power, but our minds have to be ready for it, so we need to be rehearsing it now.

precepts.text: The lights of heaven are for signs, seasons, days and years.
precepts.point: The calendar itself was changed.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Revelation 13:5 says “there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies”, and Daniel 7:25 says the same: “he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High”. Revelation 13:7 adds that “it was given unto him to make war with the saints”. The great words are things like the image of Cesare Borgia as Christ, a white man dying for the sins of everybody on the planet, getting dumped in the water to be saved, Lent, Christmas, December 25th and the rest. To wear out the saints is slavery.

“and think to change times and laws”. They changed the time with daylight saving time. They moved the beginning of the year from spring to January. Genesis 1:14 was read to show something else they changed: “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”.

Leviticus 23 shows what the seasons are for: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” The Sabbath is listed first, and it is all year round. Then come the seasonal holidays: Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, in the spring; the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth; Pentecost, counting fifty days; the blowing of trumpets on the first day of the seventh month, the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth of the seventh month; and the feast of tabernacles on the fifteenth.

Sirach 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The declaration of times is the high holy days. The lights God set in the heaven keep his calendar, and that is the calendar the beast thought to change.

precepts.text: The lesser light rules the night.
precepts.point: The calendar itself was changed.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.” The greater light is the sun and the lesser light is the moon. Notice the wording: great lights. He did not make a quarter moon or half a light. He made two great lights. What they call the full moon today is actually the new moon, and many cultures, like the Maya, hold full moon gatherings. Deuteronomy 33:14 speaks of Joseph's land and “the precious things put forth by the moon”, things that come out when the moon is at its peak, like the coquí frogs that come out under the moonlight in the islands where Ephraim and Manasseh dwell.

Sirach 43 goes on: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven”. The word month comes from moon. Every feast starts at the new moon in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom. The armies above are the armies of Revelation 19: “the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses”.

The moon is “a sign of the world”. The full moon stands for when we were in our full power and understanding. As it wanes and goes dark, that is us going into captivity, into full darkness, and when it comes back to fullness, that is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. Isaiah 60:2: “the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. When you see the dark moon, that is what it represents: we lost our heritage, and darkness covers the world.

Psalm 82 shows why: “How long will ye judge unjustly”, and because of it, “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Even the lights are out of course because of our sins. The seasons are out of order, and if the Sabbath comes every seven days, a month should have twenty-eight days. Isaiah 30:26 shows the kingdom: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases, so in the kingdom the moon will not go back into darkness. Binding up the breach is gathering the twelve tribes again, as Amos 9:11 says: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”.

precepts.text: The lights are for signs, seasons, days and years.
precepts.point: The lights of heaven set God's times, and the enemy replaced his feasts with new holidays.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Daniel 7:25 is about the white man, about Edom: “he shall speak great words against the most High”. He has called himself the people of God, called himself Christ and the people of Christ, taken God's land, said God's laws are done away with, and changed all of the Most High's holidays. “and shall wear out the saints of the most High”: he wore us out in slavery. When something is worn out it does not look the same, and that is how we forgot who we are.

“and think to change times and laws”. There is a reason it says times. Genesis 1:14: “And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. The sun and moon are set up for time. The moon is used for time, so that we can tell when our festival days come in.

Times and laws go together. Antiochus changed all our customs and made it unlawful for us to keep festival days, and America did the same thing: you do not have to keep God's feast days any more, why are you keeping Passover or Dedication, Christ did away with those things. In their place came new holidays, Christmas and Easter, our customs twisted and mixed with paganism and fed back to us. There is always a counter, good set against evil: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

It says he will think to change times and laws because he is not going to be able to. The Most High is a mastermind. He has sent his sons, his prophets, back on the earth, and they teach the right times, the feast days and God's laws. The lights he set in the heaven still keep his times.

precepts.text: God spoke from the beginning, and brought a light out of his treasures.
precepts.point: 'Let there be light' is the first thing created, the light that is Christ, before the sun and moon existed.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Ezra says the Lord spoke “from the beginning of the creation, even the first day”, saying “Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.” The word that did that perfect work is Christ.

Read on and Ezra shows what was there before anything was made: “darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed.” Nothing, a great void. “Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.” That fair light out of God’s treasures is the light of Genesis 1:3, and it is worded that way because that light is what made everything else: it came forth so that God’s works could appear.

So “in the beginning” is not only the making of the earth and the sky. It is the beginning of all creation, and it begins with Christ, the first thing God created, the light called forth on the first day.

precepts.text: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
precepts.point: 'Let there be light' is the first thing created, the light that is Christ, before the sun and moon existed.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
John opens the way Genesis does: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word that was with God is Christ. He was a God in the beginning, made in the image of his Father, creating angels, galaxies and planets. “The same was in the beginning with God”: two different persons, the Father and the Son.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Then: “In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness.” That is the same light God brought out of his treasures in 2 Esdras 6, the light of Genesis 1.

John the Baptist “came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”, and “He was not that Light.” Christ is “the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world”: the true light God created on the first day.

precepts.text: I am the light of the world.
precepts.point: 'Let there be light' is the first thing created, the light that is Christ, before the sun and moon existed.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Christ says it himself: “I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” We read that Christ is the first thing created; we go to the first thing created and God says “Let there be light”; and here Christ says, I am that light. The scriptures line up.

That is why the light of Genesis 1:3 is not the light of the sun. The earth was “without form and void”, not yet made, and the sun and moon, the “two great lights”, were not made until “the fourth day.” Read with a carnal mind, it sounds like daylight; read with the spirit, it is the Son.

Moses was told to hide these things and not make them plain for everyone, which is why Christ is called the hidden wisdom. Even the dividing of the light from the darkness, the light called day and the darkness night, is a similitude.

precepts.text: Woe unto them that put darkness for light and light for darkness.
precepts.point: Satan and evil were created too, and everything is made in pairs.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness. And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night.” Moses wrote these things the way God told him to, hiding them so that not everyone would understand. This is the first day, before the earth was created, and the first thing created was Christ. What else was created on that first day?

Isaiah 5:20 names light and darkness plainly: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Darkness is called evil and light is called good. So when the Lord divided the light from the darkness, he created good and evil. Moses is letting us know that something more is going on in Genesis 1.

On that first day spirits were created: angels were created, evil was created, Satan was created. The dividing of the light from the darkness is God choosing. The children of light are his chosen, and the rest he hardens, as the next scriptures show.

precepts.text: The Lord hardened Pharaoh.
precepts.point: Satan and evil were created too, and everything is made in pairs.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.” Read on: “His mercy is manifest to every creature; and he hath separated his light from the darkness with an adamant.” The light stands for good and the darkness for evil, and he separates them with an adamant.

The annotation in the King James gives the meaning of adamant: refusing to be persuaded, or to change one's mind. That is what the hardening of Pharaoh was. God made Pharaoh not be persuaded to let us go. That is the adamant, and that is how God separates his light from the darkness: he hardens a heart so that it will not believe and will not follow. The same way he hardened Pharaoh's heart, he will harden hearts so that people do not believe these scriptures.

So in the beginning, when God separated the light from the darkness, spirits were created, and God said: you I will choose, you are my chosen people; you I will not choose, I will harden your heart. The children of light were chosen, and the darkness was left hardened.

precepts.text: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ.
precepts.point: Satan and evil were created too, and everything is made in pairs.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. To be predestinated means you are going to get it no matter what. The definition read was: of an outcome or course of events determined in advance by divine will or fate, with the synonyms preordained, foreordained, destined, predetermined, fated, predestined.

How do you know who is predestined? You don't. Nobody today knows it. When you make it to the kingdom, that is how you know you were predestined. Read on: “To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.”

When were we predestined? When God chose to separate the light from the darkness, on the first day. Revelation 13:8 says the same thing from the other side: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” When was your name written in the book of life? From the foundation of the world. The choosing was done in the beginning, before the earth was made.

precepts.text: Ye are all the children of light and the children of the day.
precepts.point: Satan and evil were created too, and everything is made in pairs.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day”. This shows when the children of light were created. In Genesis 1 it was not only the light that was created; the light's children were created too. Christ said that he and the children are one. We were already in Christ, and when that light was formed we were in it. Then the Father chose: those on the right side are his children, and those on the left side, the two-thirds and those heathens over there, are the darkness.

God called the light Day, so we are the children of the day. That is why Day and Night are capitalized in the King James: a specific day and a specific night, good and evil, right angels and wrong ones, right spirits and wrong spirits. The apostles understood these things, and the translators did too. The spirit was on them as well when they put it in English; that council was divinely inspired. It wasn't regular men. Some of y'all dumb negroes don't speak a word of Hebrew and are trying to insult them; you're not on their level at all whatsoever. “we are not of the night, nor of darkness.” Day and night compare good and evil and the children of each, and all of that took place on the first day.

Paul goes on: “Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night. But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation. For God hath not appointed us to wrath”. We should not be sleeping; we have to be aware of the time we are living in. God did not appoint us to wrath because we are the children of the day, the children of the light.

Who is the day? 2 Peter 1:19: “a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place, and the day star arising in our hearts is Christ. He is the day.

2 Esdras 9 shows the children of light before the earth: “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed”. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic, celestial bodies, the body we will have when Christ returns, and we all obeyed. “but now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”. Covered in this flesh, we became rebellious. Knowing who we were is meant to give us the faith and hope to endure in this truth.

precepts.text: All things are double one against another, and he hath made nothing imperfect.
precepts.point: Satan and evil were created too, and everything is made in pairs.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.” Everything is made in pairs. When God divided the light from the darkness he made good and evil as a pair, and Satan and evil were created too. Nothing got into creation by mistake. There is always a counter, good set against evil all the time: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

Look at what Genesis 1 mentions first, before the earth was formed: the waters of the deep, which is space, covered in darkness. Darkness is mentioned before the light because the Lord had it set from the beginning that, when we came down here, we would be evil anyway.

That is why “the evening and the morning were the first day”: the evening comes before the morning. That is why Cain was born first, Ishmael came before Isaac, and Esau, Edom, was born before Jacob. The evil, the darkness, goes first, and then the light comes after, which is why Christ said the first shall be last and the last shall be first. The double of Sirach, darkness set against light, runs through all of Genesis.

precepts.text: Paradise, which thy right hand had planted before ever the earth came forward.
precepts.point: Time on earth began with the sun and moon on the fourth day, but with God a day is as a thousand years.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.” The waters under the firmament are the sea; the waters above are in space. There are different waters above the firmament: drink that water and you are good for eternity. Moses is writing in a similitude. “And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.” On the second day the firmament was created, and paradise, which is also called heaven, was created too.

The earth came after. “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth”. There was no shape or form down here yet. The earth was made on the third day, with the grass, the herbs and the fruit trees.

2 Esdras 3 confirms the order: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was created in the beginning, but before the earth came forth, so it was made on the second day.

This is why the class kept saying Genesis has levels. When Genesis says God made the heaven, it is not only the sky over this earth. Paradise was planted by God's right hand before the earth appeared, and Adam was led into it.

precepts.text: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years.
precepts.point: Time on earth began with the sun and moon on the fourth day, but with God a day is as a thousand years.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Our minds are earthly minds. Reading first, second and third day, we think of twenty-four hours. But when Christ was created, the earth had not been created. The sun and the moon had not been created. So did twenty-four hours exist? No.

“But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” This is saying that our time and God's time are not the same. Don't sit down and say God created the earth in seven thousand years. It only means that time with God is different; in that realm, time is not the same.

So to explain it to our human minds, Moses said first day, second day, third day. The best way to understand it is: the first thing God did, the second thing, the third, the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and then the seventh. What came out of the Father's mouth, Christ did. And it had to be given to us in human terms, because the Sabbath is counted from the creation account. If it had been given in God's terms, we would be lost and think every Sabbath comes every thousand years. He rested on the seventh day, so you rest too.

Moses saw these secrets, and God told him to write them but to hide certain things. Unless God's Spirit is in you, you will not understand them, even when they are taught to you.

precepts.text: The high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity.
precepts.point: Time on earth began with the sun and moon on the fourth day, but with God a day is as a thousand years.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy”. The high and lofty One is the Father, and he dwells in eternity. Christ was with him in eternity in the beginning; the Word was with God. Christ did not create everything all at once on the first day. The Lord told him what to do, and he did it. Christ learned from his Father: what he saw his Father do, he was able to do.

“I dwell in the high and holy place”: that is above the heavens, above paradise, the holy of holies, the fourth floor, with restricted access. No man has been up there. He dwells there “with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.”

Sirach 18 explains eternity: “The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years. As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.” In eternity, where the Father is, a thousand years is like nothing. Those are the days of the Ancient of days. Sirach 1:2 says the same: “Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?” No one can count God's days. He exists outside of time, before time.

This goes with what Peter said: the days of Genesis are not earth days. They are measured from where the Father dwells, in eternity.

precepts.text: He hangeth the earth upon nothing.
precepts.point: Time on earth began with the sun and moon on the fourth day, but with God a day is as a thousand years.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
With a picture of the earth in space on the screen, 2 Esdras 16 was read: “He searcheth the deep, and the treasures thereof; he hath measured the sea, and what it containeth. He hath shut the sea in the midst of the waters, and with his word hath he hanged the earth upon the waters.” All around the earth is space, and the earth hangs in it like an ornament the Lord just hung there. The water it hangs on is space. Astronauts train in the water because that is where they are going; spend too long in space and your bones get brittle, just as they get crushed if you go too deep under water.

Job calls that water something else: “He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.” When you see the earth in space, it is on nothing. You cannot see any water, but the water is there surrounding it. The nothing is the water.

So why doesn't the earth move and float off one way or another? That is the Most High showing his power. 2 Esdras 16:59: “He spreadeth out the heavens like a vault; upon the waters hath he founded it.” A vault is an arch; it goes around, it is round, not flat. Founded means established: the earth stays in the spot where he founded it, while the sun moves. The devil says the opposite, that the earth moves; but God said the earth is founded, and it stays there. This is the same work as Genesis 1:6, where the firmament was set in the midst of the waters.

precepts.text: God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.
precepts.point: 'Replenish' means to fill again, and Adam was told to subdue the earth.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Genesis 1 is an abbreviation, and Genesis 2 explains it, the same way Genesis 10 mentions Babel and Genesis 11 explains why it is called Babel. When Genesis 1:27 says “male and female created he them”, Genesis 2 shows how he did it.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”. The dust of the ground is brown: Adam was a black man, and he wasn't walking around butt naked on earth. “and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”: when he breathed into him, he put that spirit inside him, the spirit that is his Son from the beginning. “and man became a living soul.” That is how Adam was created.

Then Eve: “And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” Eve was created from Adam, and Adam from the ground.

2 Esdras 3 tells the same story and goes further: God breathed into Adam the breath of life, “and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth. He and his wife were the only flesh that could go there, until he sinned. That is why flesh and blood cannot be up there: flesh and blood has that sinful nature. The man who could walk into paradise wasn't running around butt naked. He was ruling.

precepts.text: God created man to be immortal and made him an image of his own eternity.
precepts.point: 'Replenish' means to fill again, and Adam was told to subdue the earth.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
What does it mean when the Lord says, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”? Wisdom of Solomon 2:23: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” That is how Adam was created before he sinned: immortal. Being in God's image is not only about how we look. It goes into his power and his divinity too.

2 Esdras 8:44 says man “is called thine own image, because thou art like unto him, for whose sake thou hast made all things”. Adam was just like his father, the way someone says, you are just like your father, you are the image of your father. We are supposed to be in the image of Christ, and Christ is in the image of the Father. All things were created for Adam and for the sons of Adam, which is us. Not everyone was created in Adam's image; the sons of God are the ones created in Adam's image, because Adam was created in God's image.

“and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That is the kingdom of Adam, in so many words. Then in verse 28 God tells them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it”. To replenish means to fill something up again. There is a big gap after verse 27: a lot of time went by. Why would God tell Adam to subdue the earth if he already had dominion over it? That was left to be answered later in the class.

Deuteronomy 11:21 shows Moses saw Adam's kingdom: keep the commandments in the land, and your days will be “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam ruled. 2 Esdras 7:26 speaks of the bride that “now is withdrawn from the earth”: that holy city, the access to the spirit realm, withdrew itself from the earth, so it must once have been on the earth, in the time of Adam. How Adam was on the earth is how we are going to be in the future.

precepts.text: The Most High commanded a fair light on the first day so that His work might appear.
precepts.point: What exactly that first light was is not declared; what is declared is that He commanded a fair light so that His work might appear. Genesis 1:1 coincides with 2 Esdras 6.

note.label: Genesis 1: The Creation of Light and Mankind

precepts.why:
Genesis 1:1 coincides with 2 Esdras 6. “O Lord, thou spakest from the beginning of the creation, even the first day, and saidst thus; Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work. And then was the spirit, and darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed. Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.”

The Most High commanded a fair light on the first day so that his work might appear. That is “Let there be light.” It came before the sun, the moon and the stars, which were not made until the fourth day; it is the light you see in the morning sky before the sun comes up. There is light in the sky when the sun is not out, and the Most High made that light first. The light is twelve hours and the darkness is twelve hours, and afterward he made the sun as the greater light to rule the day.

What exactly that first light was is not declared. What is declared is that he commanded a fair light to come forth of his treasures, that his work might appear.

precepts.text: The man made in our image, created he him, is the first Adam; male and female created he them is the other people.
precepts.point: When Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.” Then: “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Two things are said there, and Genesis 5 says them the same way: “in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them.”

The man made in our image, “created he him”, is the first Adam, made in the likeness of God, a direct descendant of the Most High. “Male and female created he them” is the other people: they were not that Adam. When the Most High creates a fish He does not create only a salmon; there is mackerel and tuna and all types of fish. In the same way, He created Adam and He created the other people, and called their name Adam in the day when they were created.

precepts.text: Every herb bearing seed and every tree yielding seed, to you it shall be for meat; meat does not have to be an animal.
precepts.point: Meat in the scriptures is not always talking about animals. Every tree yielding seed was given for meat; the inside of a fruit is called the meat of that fruit, the meat of an orange, an apple, a pear, a watermelon.

note.label: Leviticus 2: The Meat Offering of Fine Flour

precepts.why:
Leviticus 2:7 always goes viral on social media, as if the meat offering baken in the fryingpan relates to fried chicken. That is not what it is talking about. The chapter itself defines the meat: go back to verse 1, and the offering is of fine flour, not fried chicken. When you have questions, go back to the beginning verses of the chapter and you get the true understanding.

Meat in the scriptures is not always talking about animals. “Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.” Herbs and fruit are called meat. The inside of a fruit is called the meat of that fruit: the meat of an orange, an apple, a pear, a watermelon.

So a meat offering “made of fine flour with oil” is meat in that sense. Be mindful of learning from posts instead of from the scriptures.

precepts.text: The lights in the firmament were made for signs and for seasons, the lesser light to rule the night, on the fourth day; the moon came after the week was already counting.
precepts.point: If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
The moon governs the months and the feasts, but it has nothing to do with the seventh day Sabbath. The lights in the firmament were made “for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”, “the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”, and “the evening and the morning were the fourth day.”

The moon was not created on the first day of the week but on the fourth. The week was already counting, day one, day two, day three, before the moon existed. So the moon cannot set the Sabbath; the seven day rotation has run since the first day and nothing changes it.

The day starts at evening, for the evening and the morning were the day; darkness was here first and has seniority. The Sabbath will always be Friday sundown to Saturday sundown.

precepts.text: The evening and the morning were the first day; the day starts at evening, so the sabbath runs from even unto even.
precepts.point: From even unto even shall ye celebrate your sabbath, the ninth day of the month at even. Even unto even is how days are numbered, one complete day of twenty-four hours, not sunrise to sunrise, for the evening and the morning were the first day.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“in the ninth day of the month at even, from even unto even, shall ye celebrate your sabbath.” Even unto even is how days are numbered: “And the evening and the morning were the first day.”

The day starts at evening. So the day of atonement is one complete day of twenty-four hours from sundown on the ninth to sundown on the tenth, not sunrise to sunrise, and every sabbath runs the same way, from even unto even.

precepts.text: God called the dry land earth; through the Lord's hand He made all things.
precepts.point: The sea is His, He made it, and His hands formed the dry land. Through the Lord's hand He made all things.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land.” Genesis shows the day he did it: “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.”

God called the dry land Earth and the gathering together of the waters Seas. Through the Lord's hand he made all things. The sea is his because he made it, and the dry land is his because his hands formed it, along with the deep places of the earth and the strength of the hills, the strength being their height.

precepts.text: The lights of heaven are for signs and seasons, days and years.
precepts.point: He makes His angels spirits and His ministers a flaming fire.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain”. The Most High stretched out the heavens, and he set the lights in them.
